title: Incremental token escrow rehydration and fallthrough mediator
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Problem: Late-arriving consumption events and intermittent edge replays are causing small but material underruns in tenant token balances and skewed per-route billing. Existing epochal compactor jobs fix large drifts but are too heavyweight for near-real-time corrections and cause invoice surprises when applied retroactively.

Goal: Implement an incremental token escrow rehydration worker that continuously ingests late events, merges them into a lightweight escrow state, and emits deterministic correction deltas with strong idempotency guarantees. The worker should act as a fallthrough mediator when the primary real-time ledger is missing events, and produce bounded, backfillable corrections that the billing pipeline can consume without large reprocessing windows.
design_summary:
Architecture: a stateful streaming worker that subscribes to the event topic (kafka: consumption-events-late) and a compacted escrow changelog. The worker maintains per-tenant, per-route escrow windows keyed by (tenant_id, route_id, epoch_bucket). It computes correction deltas, writes them to a compacted corrections topic, and concurrently updates a lightweight checkpoint store (DynamoDB) for idempotency. For heavier cross-epoch merges the worker triggers a snapshot export picked up by the epochal compactor.

Key properties: strictly monotonic correction sequence numbers, at-least-once ingestion tolerance with dedup via deterministic event fingerprints, bounded memory via TTL and reservoir sampling for very high-cardinality tenants, and graceful degradation path (emit tombstone deltas and route to slow-path backfill) when faced with GC pressure.
steps: Draft design doc and consensus (Confluence link in 'links')
Build streaming worker scaffold (Go) with Kafka consumer groups and consistent sharding by (tenant_id % N)
Implement deterministic fingerprinting for events and per-event sequence stabilization
Checkpointing: DynamoDB write-after-emit pattern and audit log for at-most-once downstream replay
Add backfill tool to rehydrate escrow windows from S3 event snapshots for customers with large late windows
Integrate corrections topic into billing ingestion; add warnings and compensating allowance in invoicing microservice
Canary deploy to staging, run synthetic late-arrival scenarios, and validate Grafana metrics and dashboards
Roll forward to prod with progressive traffic ramp and a rollback playbook
acceptance_criteria: Worker stabilizes and processes sustained 30k late events/sec in staging without OOMs
Per-tenant correction churn is <0.2% of daily usage for tenants under normal latency profiles
All emitted correction deltas include monotonic sequence and idempotency key; replaying the same stream yields no double-credit
Billing ingestion accepts corrections topic with <2s processing latency under canary load
Runbook validated: abort, drain, and manual rehydrate steps tested end-to-end
No customer-facing invoice deltas outside the window defined in the billing policy (configurable, default 7 days)
comments: 2026-02-22 - Aisha Kapoor: Initial spike showed memory blowup for top-100 tenants. Decided to add reservoir sampling + per-tenant soft limit rather than global heap reservation.
2026-02-28 - Miguel Santos: Implemented deterministic fingerprinting prototype (sha256(event_key | timestamp_window)). Benchmarked dedup cost: ~0.5ms/event on p3-standard; acceptable.
2026-03-03 - PM review (Jordan Li): Ask to surface 'explainability' field in correction deltas for SRE and customer support to understand why credits were applied.
2026-03-06 - Design feedback (Priya Menon): Prefer DynamoDB conditional writes for checkpointing to avoid compaction races. Also add a compacted tombstone emitter for route decommissioning.
2026-03-10 - Engineering update: End-to-end canary in staging processed 120k late events over 24h; observed 0.03% duplication which was eliminated by tightening fingerprint window boundaries.
2026-03-11 - Security: quick review notes no PII in corrections payload; recommended masking of any free-form prompt text before emitting to corrections topic.
2026-03-12 - Miguel Santos: Draft PR posted; integration tests failing intermittently on CI due to race in checkpoint TTL cleanup. Next action: add lease-based cleanup and retry backoff.
